subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `direct.*.tools` and `direct.*.toolsBySender` be a supported DM enforcement contract, or should OpenClaw reject/diagnose that config as unsupported?
rationale: The current schema and types accept the field, but changing enforcement affects a security-sensitive tool-permission boundary and must preserve sender/account precedence rather than landing a one-sided resolver change.

options.title: Enforce direct tool policy
options.body: Treat the accepted config as a supported contract and add a DM-aware resolver with Telegram regression coverage and live proof.

options.title: Retire the accepted surface
options.body: Make schema, doctor, docs, and diagnostics reject or warn on direct tool-policy config so operators cannot assume enforcement that does not exist.

recommendation.title: Enforce direct tool policy
recommendation.body: Treat the accepted config as a supported contract and add a DM-aware resolver with Telegram regression coverage and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and current shallow blame point to this person as the strongest owner for the shared policy/security boundary decision.
